fact_text: An estimate cited in the video puts what Pakistani freelancers earn from foreign clients at roughly $700 million to $1 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: Remittances flowing into Pakistan run at about $3 billion a month, according to the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: The video describes Pakistan as the fourth-largest freelancing market in the world.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: International payment firms usually charge three kinds of fees: a per-transaction fee, an FX conversion margin, and platform fees such as registration, monthly, yearly or inactivity charges.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: Many platforms advertise zero transaction fees but, according to the video, charge 4 to 5 percent, and in some cases up to 8 percent, on the currency conversion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: Freelancers complain that payment platform fee structures are not transparent and that firms raise charges without telling customers, as the video's guests argued.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: Company payments in Pakistan typically take about a week to a week and a half to process, according to the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: After the freelancing boom of 2006 to 2010, rival countries shifted focus to companies, SMEs and product development, which the video says is why Pakistan's freelancing is not recognised as scalable.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: Global payment firms are seen as deterred by a long history of currency problems, a regulatory regime that does not fit their business plans, and the need for a clear exit route for investors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: Successive governments, from the PTI government to PML-N, tried to bring PayPal into Pakistan, and none of the attempts succeeded.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: The video argues Pakistan's payment regulation needs fundamental changes before it can invite many international fintechs to operate in the country.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: Several new payment players, including Tap and Remitly, have entered Pakistan's payments ecosystem, and some local banks have started freelancer remittance services.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: The reporter expects at least three new payment firms to enter Pakistan in 2026, and says some already have a head start on State Bank processes.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)

fact_text: The reporter expects that with regulator support Pakistan can settle company payments in a much shorter time in 2026, and says payment speed is a competitive factor.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan's Payment Dilemma: Billions of Dollars, Few Gateways | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-20)
